argument_summary: The defensible position is narrower than clean certification. The admissible record supports an audit packet that rejects any claim of 'no material weakness,' affirms aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and conditions the certification defense on explicit disclosure of the unresolved childcare subsidy eligibility limitation and the fact that the proposed mitigation remains unapproved. On that framing, the packet is not using the draft runbook to cure the weakness; it is using the existing evidence to support a caveated certification record.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is needed to support this position, and none is relied upon.
claims_about_policy: The policy text clearly does two things on this record: it forecloses certification without material caveats unless the weakness is resolved or covered by an approved mitigation, and it requires disclosure of a material limitation for a named launch use case unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The packet we are defending should therefore be evaluated as caveated compliance, not as a claim of clean compliance. I am not claiming the record expressly proves unrestricted certification authority; I am claiming the admissible evidence supports a certification packet only if it is narrowed to disclose the limitation, acknowledge the draft status of mitigation, and avoid representing the release as free of material caveats.
concessions: The admissible record does not show an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
The current draft model card is internally inconsistent because it says there are no known material limitations while the childcare subsidy eligibility issue remains unresolved.
The record does not contain an explicit admissible materiality determination or express policy text affirmatively authorizing certification despite the unresolved slice.
The draft runbook cannot be treated as curing the present weakness under the supplied policy standard.
